# NPCs

Read the `npcs` doc (`read_doc`, slug `npcs`) and follow the `add-npcs` playbook (`get_playbook`, name `add-npcs`).

## Order of work

1. **Scripted baseline first.** A good state machine or utility AI that works with no model, offline. It is the `fallback`, and it runs instantly whenever the platform cannot answer (budget, rate limit, timeout, error, standalone, disabled). Verification runs the game with every model disabled and rejects broken NPCs.
2. Only then consider model decisions. If the scripted NPC is already good, stop.
3. Declare a **brain** in `osg.json` (`features.npcs.brains`): `id`, `question`, optional `persona`, and 1-32 `options` (label to description). They are fixed per version; the game sends only the brain id.
4. Use `osg.npcs.createBrain` with `npcs`, `world`, a REQUIRED `fallback(id)` returning an option label, and `onDecision`. Default cadence is one call per 1.5 s; never below 500 ms.
5. **Batch**: one call, one shared `world`, up to 8 NPCs. Never a call per NPC.
6. **Gate on confidence** (start at 0.5) and re-validate every choice against the game rules before acting.

## `world` hygiene

JSON under 4 KiB. Positions, distances, scores, flags. **Never** chat text, player names or any player-typed text, secrets, tokens or personal data.

## NPC seats

NPC seats are driven by the host's client (`osg.npcs.add()` as host, needs `features.rooms` and `npcs.seats`). They never reach boards or achievements. A hidden host tab freezes them.

## Say honestly

The model that answers can change and may be small; budgets are finite; the fallback running is normal. Do not write copy or design that needs a particular intelligence.
